import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Battery-feasibility-adjusted arrival: net value after decay, gated by whether the flight can be made without running out."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    is_charger = values <= 0
    # time to reach, plus charging time if we end at charger
    travel = d
    # effective arrival value after decay during flight (never below 0)
    life = np.where(rates > 0, values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9), np.inf)
    arrival_val = np.maximum(values - rates * travel, 0.0)
    # feasibility: does the flight fit in the battery?
    need = d * drain
    feasible = (need <= battery).astype(float)
    # for charger candidate, treat as always feasible with value scaled by urgency (low battery good)
    charger_score = is_charger.astype(float) * (1.0 - battery)
    # normalise arrival value
    scale = np.maximum(values.max(), 1e-9)
    item_score = np.where(is_charger, 0.0, arrival_val / scale) * feasible
    return item_score + charger_score

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Arrival value amortised over the full battery cycle: flight out plus the trip back to the charger (and recharge time) needed to keep flying, so candidates far from the charger or draining a lot of battery are discounted; charger scores 1 - battery."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    is_charger = values <= 0
    d_charger = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)
    # total flight path if we go to the item and then must return to the charger
    tour = d + d_charger
    # battery spent on that tour
    spent = np.clip(tour * drain, 0.0, None)
    # recharge time needed to recover what was spent (after arriving at the charger)
    recharge = np.clip(spent / max(charge_rate, 1e-9), 0.0, None)
    # full cycle time: out, back, recharge
    cycle = tour + recharge
    # arrival value after decay during the outbound flight only
    arrival_val = np.maximum(values - rates * d, 0.0)
    # amortise over the cycle, guarding division
    eff = arrival_val / np.maximum(cycle, 1e-3)
    # normalise by the best achievable efficiency among items
    item_eff = np.where(is_charger, 0.0, eff)
    scale = np.maximum(item_eff.max(), 1e-9)
    # feasibility gate for the outbound leg
    feasible = (d * drain <= battery + 1e-9).astype(float)
    item_score = (item_eff / scale) * feasible
    charger_score = is_charger.astype(float) * (1.0 - battery)
    return item_score + charger_score

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Negative shortfall of the out-and-back trip measured in recharge-time units (how long you'd be stuck recharging), gated to items only; zero for the charger and zero when the trip is affordable."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    dch = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)
    need = (d + dch) * drain
    shortfall_batt = np.maximum(need - battery, 0.0)
    # convert the battery shortfall into the wall-clock time it costs to recover it
    stuck_time = shortfall_batt / max(charge_rate, 1e-9)
    # also add the raw flight time that the shortfall implies (must detour via charger)
    extra_fly = shortfall_batt / max(drain, 1e-9)
    cost = stuck_time + extra_fly
    # normalise by a soft time scale: the whole horizon + a floor
    scale = max(time_left, 1.0) + 1.0
    feat = -np.clip(cost / scale, 0.0, 1.0)
    is_item = values > 0
    return np.where(is_item, feat, 0.0)

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Max-decayed-value of any single other item reachable after picking this candidate (battery after arrival, then detour to that item and back to charger), minus the value-at-risk of the chosen candidate; charger row uses 1 - battery."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)          # pos -> each candidate
    is_item = values > 0
    D = np.linalg.norm(targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :], axis=2)  # candidate -> other
    dch = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)    # candidate -> charger
    b_after = battery - d * drain                               # battery at each candidate
    # reachability from candidate i to other item j and back to charger
    trip = D + dch[None, :]                                     # (i,j)
    reach = (b_after[:, None] - trip * drain) > 0
    reach &= is_item[None, :]
    np.fill_diagonal(reach, False)
    # decayed value of j at time we'd get there (via i)
    vj = np.maximum(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * (d[:, None] + D), 0.0)
    # best single follow-up item (not sum) -> focuses on the next good move
    masked = np.where(reach, vj, 0.0)
    best_follow = masked.max(axis=1) if masked.size else np.zeros(len(targets))
    norm = max(values.max(), 1e-9)
    follow = best_follow / norm

    # value-at-risk of the chosen candidate itself (how much it decays before arrival)
    arrival = np.maximum(values - rates * d, 0.0)
    risk = np.where(is_item, 1.0 - arrival / np.maximum(values, 1e-9), 0.0)

    item_score = np.clip(follow * 0.7 - risk * 0.5, -1.0, 1.0)
    charger_score = (~is_item).astype(float) * (1.0 - battery)
    return np.where(is_item, item_score, charger_score)

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Min over the two legs of the best pair (c then j) of the slack life - travel time, clipped and zero for the charger."""
    k = targets.shape[0]
    is_item = values > 0
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)  # (k,)
    diff = targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :]     # (k, k, 2)
    D = np.linalg.norm(diff, axis=2)                     # (k, k)
    life = values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9)              # (k,)
    slack1 = life - d                                    # (k,)
    second = life[None, :] - (d[:, None] + D)            # (k, k)
    masked = np.where(np.eye(k, dtype=bool), -1e9, np.minimum(slack1[:, None], second))
    pair = masked.max(axis=1)                            # (k,)
    return np.where(is_item, np.clip(pair / 3.0, -1.0, 1.0), 0.0)

feature.name: endgame_surviving_density
feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Endgame density of value that still survives to arrival, minus the unreachable overshoot: arrival value per unit time-to-reach, weighted by how much of the item's remaining life the trip consumes, zero outside the last stretch before the end."""
    k = targets.shape[0]
    is_item = values > 0
    d1 = np.sqrt(((targets - pos) ** 2).sum(axis=1))
    travel = np.maximum(d1, 1e-3)
    arrival = np.maximum(values - rates * travel, 0.0)
    # does the trip even finish before the episode ends? if not, it collects nothing
    finishes = (travel <= time_left).astype(float)
    # how much of the item's remaining life the trip eats (urgency)
    life = np.where(rates > 0, values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9), 1e9)
    life_share = np.clip(travel / np.maximum(life, 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    # density: surviving value per unit of time spent flying there, boosted when the trip eats the item's life
    dens = (arrival / travel) * (1.0 + life_share) * finishes
    dens = np.where(is_item, dens, 0.0)
    dens = np.where(np.isfinite(dens), dens, 0.0)
    dmax = dens.max() if k > 0 else 0.0
    # gate: only in the endgame window, and only meaningful if something is still capturable
    window = np.clip((8.0 - time_left) / 8.0, 0.0, 1.0)
    if dmax > 0.0 and window > 0.0:
        out = (dens / dmax) * window
    else:
        out = np.zeros(k)
    out = np.where(is_item, out, 0.0)
    return np.nan_to_num(out, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
feature.measures: Endgame density of value that still survives to arrival, minus the unreachable overshoot: arrival value per unit time-to-reach, weighted by how much of the item's remaining life the trip consumes, zero outside the last stretch before the end.

feature.name: perishable_windowed_value_rate
feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Affordable-value-rate but as a *two-hop* efficiency: value that survives arrival relative to the time until it would actually be gone (min(life, trip+buffer)), gated by affordability and by whether the item dies before we could get there."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    is_charger = values <= 0
    # value surviving the outbound flight
    arrival = np.maximum(values - rates * d, 0.0)
    # affordability fraction, but use the fraction of the *reserve* (battery beyond a safety margin)
    margin = 0.15
    spare = np.maximum(battery - margin, 0.0)
    need = d * drain
    afford = np.clip(1.0 - need / np.maximum(spare, 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    # remaining life of the item (time until it disappears)
    life = np.where(rates > 0, values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9), 1e9)
    # effective window: how long the item is actually still worth anything to us
    window = np.minimum(life, np.maximum(time_left, 0.0))
    # will it still be alive on arrival at all?
    alive = (d < life).astype(float)
    # efficiency: surviving value per unit of the (short) window we get to exploit it
    eff = arrival / np.maximum(window, 0.2)
    # boost when the trip eats most of the item's remaining life (last-chance urgency)
    perish = np.clip(d / np.maximum(life, 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    s = eff * afford * alive * (1.0 + perish)
    item_scale = np.maximum(s[~is_charger].max() if np.any(~is_charger) else 1e-9, 1e-9)
    s = s / item_scale
    return np.where(is_charger, 0.0, np.nan_to_num(s, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0))
feature.measures: Affordable-value-rate but as a *two-hop* efficiency: value that survives arrival relative to the time until it would actually be gone (min(life, trip+buffer)), gated by affordability and by whether the item dies before we could get there.

feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Best follow-up item reachable after this one, but discounted by the total decay (of both this item and the follow-up) and by how much of the follow-up's remaining life the chained trip eats; charger row uses 1 - battery."""
    k = targets.shape[0]
    is_item = values > 0
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)                 # pos -> candidate
    D = np.linalg.norm(targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :], axis=2)  # candidate -> other
    dch = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)           # candidate -> charger
    b_after = battery - d * drain
    life = np.where(rates > 1e-12, values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9), 1e9)  # remaining life

    # battery reachability for chained trip i -> j -> charger
    trip = D + dch[None, :]
    reach = (b_after[:, None] - trip * drain) > 0
    reach &= is_item[None, :]
    np.fill_diagonal(reach, False)

    # time to fly pos->i->j
    t_arrive_j = d[:, None] + D
    # decayed value of j at that time
    vj = np.maximum(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * t_arrive_j, 0.0)
    # how much of j's life the chained trip eats: high when we barely make it
    life_share = np.clip(t_arrive_j / np.maximum(life[None, :], 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    # boost follow-ups that are near expiry along the chain (urgent to grab next)
    vj_urgent = vj * (1.0 + 0.5 * life_share)
    masked = np.where(reach, vj_urgent, 0.0)
    best_follow = masked.max(axis=1) if masked.size else np.zeros(k)

    # also account for candidate's own decay before arrival and for whether it even arrives in time
    arrival_i = np.maximum(values - rates * d, 0.0)
    finishes_i = (d <= time_left).astype(float)
    own_decay_frac = np.where(is_item, 1.0 - arrival_i / np.maximum(values, 1e-9), 0.0)

    norm = max(values.max(), 1e-9)
    follow = best_follow / norm
    # combine: follow-up value that survives, minus own decay, gated on arrival
    item_score = finishes_i * (follow - own_decay_frac)
    item_score = np.clip(item_score, -1.0, 1.0)

    charger_score = (~is_item).astype(float) * (1.0 - battery)
    return np.where(is_item, item_score, charger_score)

feature.name: inflicted_decay_detour_tax
feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Detour tax on *surviving value of others*: for each candidate i, sum over other items j of (value_j that survives the extra detour via i) x (that detour), normalised by total surviving value; charger gets the min item score."""
    k = targets.shape[0]
    is_item = values > 0
    d1 = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)             # (k,) pos->i
    D = np.linalg.norm(targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :], axis=2)  # (k,k) i->j
    # extra distance to reach j if we visit i first vs going straight from pos
    detour = np.maximum(d1[:, None] + D - d1[None, :], 0.0)        # (k,k)
    # how much of j's value is still alive when we finally get there via i
    remaining_life_j = values[None, :] / np.maximum(rates[None, :], 1e-9)  # (1,k)
    time_via_i = d1[:, None] + D                                   # (k,k)
    alive = np.maximum(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * time_via_i, 0.0)  # (k,k)
    # value actually lost to j's decay that is *caused* by the detour (extra time beyond direct)
    direct_alive = np.maximum(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * d1[None, :], 0.0)  # (1,k)
    lost = np.maximum(direct_alive - alive, 0.0)                   # (k,k)
    # tax = value lost on all other items due to detouring through i, weighted by detour length
    eye = np.eye(k, dtype=bool)
    lost = np.where(eye, 0.0, lost)
    detour = np.where(eye, 0.0, detour)
    item_w = np.where(is_item, 1.0, 0.0)[None, :]
    tax = (lost * item_w + 1e-3 * detour * np.where(is_item, rates, 0.0)[None, :] * item_w).sum(axis=1)
    # normalise by total currently-alive value of items, so scale-free
    total_val = np.maximum(values[is_item].sum(), 1e-9) if np.any(is_item) else 1.0
    score = -np.clip(tax / total_val, 0.0, 1.0)                    # negative: taxing others is bad
    score = np.where(is_item, score, 0.0)
    if np.any(is_item):
        charger_score = float(np.max(score[is_item]))              # charger = best (least harmful) option
    else:
        charger_score = 0.0
    return np.where(is_item, score, charger_score)

feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """For the charger row: value of waiting (battery deficit and time-left), blended with the best nearby item's surviving value so waiting only wins when the charger is a genuine hub; items score 0."""
    k = targets.shape[0]
    is_charger = values <= 0
    # best surviving item value from the charger's perspective
    d_ch = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)
    survive = np.maximum(values - rates * d_ch, 0.0)
    survive = np.where(is_charger, 0.0, survive)
    best_from_charger = survive.max() if k > 0 else 0.0
    norm = max(values.max(), 1e-9)
    # how much battery we are missing (waiting is more useful when empty)
    deficit = 1.0 - battery
    # time cost to recharge
    recharge_t = deficit / max(charge_rate, 1e-9)
    # waiting is attractive if recharge is quick relative to remaining horizon
    quick = np.clip(1.0 - recharge_t / max(time_left, 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    # hub bonus: many/valuable items near the charger
    hub = np.clip(best_from_charger / norm, 0.0, 1.0)
    charger_score = quick * (0.5 + 0.5 * hub) * deficit
    out = np.where(is_charger, charger_score, 0.0)
    return np.nan_to_num(out, nan=0.0, posinf=1.0, neginf=-1.0)

feature.name: three_leg_chain_value
feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Three-leg chain: best (v_i + v_j + v_k) over feasible i->j->k->charger chains, normalised by best arrival value."""
    k = targets.shape[0]
    is_item = values > 0
    eps = 1e-6

    # d1: drone -> candidate i
    d1 = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)  # (k,)
    # arrival value at i
    v_i = np.maximum(values - rates * d1, 0.0)
    # leg-1 feasibility: pos -> i -> charger within battery
    d_i_charger = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)
    leg1_ok = (drain * (d1 + d_i_charger) <= battery) & is_item

    # pairwise distances i -> j
    diff = targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :]  # (k,k,2)
    d_ij = np.linalg.norm(diff, axis=2)  # (k,k)
    # arrival value at j given we went pos->i->j
    t_ij = d1[:, None] + d_ij  # (k,k)
    v_j = np.maximum(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * t_ij, 0.0)  # (k,k)
    # leg feasibility for i->j->charger
    leg2_ok = (drain * (t_ij + d_i_charger[None, :]) <= battery) & is_item[None, :]
    # exclude j == i
    same_ij = np.eye(k, dtype=bool)
    leg2_ok = leg2_ok & ~same_ij

    # A = v_i + best v_j over feasible j
    v_j_masked = np.where(leg2_ok, v_j, 0.0)
    best_vj = v_j_masked.max(axis=1)  # (k,)
    has_j = leg2_ok.any(axis=1)
    A = v_i + best_vj

    # For B we need, for each i, the j achieving best_vj, then best k from that j.
    # Use argmax over masked v_j.
    j_idx = v_j_masked.argmax(axis=1)  # (k,)
    # time at j: t_ij[i, j_idx[i]]
    t_at_j = t_ij[np.arange(k), j_idx]  # (k,)
    # distances j -> k for each i: d_ij[i, j_idx[i]] then j->k
    d_ij_sel = d_ij[np.arange(k), j_idx]  # (k,)
    # j position for each i
    j_pos = targets[j_idx]  # (k,2)
    # distances from selected j to every k
    diff_jk = j_pos[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :]  # (k,k,2)
    d_jk = np.linalg.norm(diff_jk, axis=2)  # (k,k)
    t_ijk = t_at_j[:, None] + d_jk  # (k,k)
    v_k = np.maximum(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * t_ijk, 0.0)  # (k,k)
    # feasibility: drain*(d1 + d_ij + d_jk + |k-charger|) <= battery
    leg3_ok = (drain * (t_ijk + d_i_charger[None, :]) <= battery) & is_item[None, :]
    # exclude k == i and k == j
    idx_range = np.arange(k)
    leg3_ok = leg3_ok & ~(idx_range[:, None] == idx_range[None, :])  # k != i
    leg3_ok = leg3_ok & ~(j_idx[:, None] == idx_range[None, :])  # k != j
    v_k_masked = np.where(leg3_ok, v_k, 0.0)
    B = v_k_masked.max(axis=1)  # (k,)
    B = np.where(has_j, B, 0.0)

    chain = A + B
    chain = np.where(leg1_ok, chain, 0.0)

    # normaliser: max over items of v_i (arrival value)
    norm = v_i[is_item].max() if is_item.any() else 0.0
    score = np.clip(chain / (norm + eps), 0.0, 3.0)
    # charger row: 1 - battery
    score = np.where(is_item, score, 1.0 - battery)
    return score

feature.name: burst_weighted_recharge_density
feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Arrival value per (flight time + 3*burst*recharge time), normalised by the max over items; charger row = 1 - battery."""
    k = targets.shape[0]
    is_item = values > 0

    # Burst signal from history appearance times (column 2).
    s = history.shape[0]
    if s > 0:
        recent = np.count_nonzero(history[:, 2] >= time - 10.0)
    else:
        recent = 0
    lam_recent = recent / 10.0
    lam_ref = (s + 1.0) / (time + 1.0)
    burst = np.clip((lam_recent - lam_ref) / (lam_ref + 0.2), 0.0, 1.0)

    # Per-candidate geometry.
    diff = targets - pos[None, :]
    travel = np.maximum(np.sqrt(np.sum(diff * diff, axis=1)), 1e-3)
    to_charger = np.sqrt(np.sum((targets - charger[None, :]) ** 2, axis=1))

    arrival = np.maximum(values - rates * travel, 0.0)
    recharge_time = drain * (travel + to_charger) / max(charge_rate, 1e-6)
    denom = travel + 3.0 * burst * recharge_time
    raw = arrival / np.maximum(denom, 1e-6)

    # Normalise by max raw over items.
    item_raw = np.where(is_item, raw, -np.inf)
    max_raw = np.max(item_raw) if np.any(is_item) else 0.0
    if not np.isfinite(max_raw):
        max_raw = 0.0
    score = np.where(is_item, raw / (max_raw + 1e-6), 0.0)

    # Charger row.
    score = np.where(is_item, score, 1.0 - battery)
    return score

idea.hypothesis: Recharge time is invisible to f012, which divides by flight time only; it is exactly the cost that hurts in waves (26% charger time). During a burst of appearances the price of a long recharge rises because the drone is off the board while items arrive and decay. Weighting the recharge component by a burst signal read off history (appearance rate in the last 10 time units against the average rate) should shift the choice toward short-recharge items exactly during bursts and change nothing during lulls.
idea.feature: history is (s,5) with appearance times in column 2. recent = count of rows with appeared_time >= time - 10; lambda_recent = recent / 10; lambda_ref = (s + 1) / (time + 1); burst = clip((lambda_recent - lambda_ref) / (lambda_ref + 0.2), 0, 1). For items: travel = max(|pos - i|, 1e-3), arrival = max(values_i - rates_i*travel, 0), recharge_time = drain*(travel + |i - charger|) / max(charge_rate, 1e-6); raw = arrival / (travel + 3*burst*recharge_time); score = raw / (max raw over items + 1e-6) (0 if no items). Charger row = 1 - battery.

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Negative clipped excess of the out-and-back battery need over 70% of the current battery (0 for the charger)."""
    pos = np.asarray(pos, dtype=float)
    targets = np.asarray(targets, dtype=float)
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    charger = np.asarray(charger, dtype=float)

    d1 = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    d_back = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)
    need = drain * (d1 + d_back)
    ratio = need / max(float(battery), 1e-6)
    score = -np.clip(ratio - 0.7, 0.0, 1.0)
    score = np.where(values == 0, 0.0, score)
    return np.nan_to_num(score, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Normalised arrival-value density tilted by a saturating function of the item's own arrival value; charger row = 1 - battery."""
    is_item = values > 0
    travel = np.maximum(np.linalg.norm(targets - pos, axis=1), 1e-3)
    arrival = np.maximum(values - rates * travel, 0.0)
    density = arrival / travel

    score = np.zeros_like(values)
    if np.any(is_item):
        arr_items = arrival[is_item]
        m = float(np.mean(arr_items))
        if m >= 1e-9:
            tilt = arrival / (arrival + m)
            max_density = float(np.max(density[is_item]))
            score = np.clip((density / (max_density + 1e-12)) * tilt, 0.0, 1.0)
    score[~is_item] = 1.0 - battery
    return score

idea.hypothesis: Pure density (f012, the whole policy) herds the drone onto cheap nearby items and lets large, slower items expire: missed_pct is 26-37% while decay_pct is only ~24%, i.e. more value is never collected than is lost in flight. Multiplying density by a saturating tilt on the item's own arrival value keeps the time-efficiency ordering but breaks ties in favour of items big enough to matter, so the large ones stop being left to die.

Charger row = 1 - battery.

system:
You are the **Navigator** in Helix, an evolutionary search. You don't write candidates. You keep the search oriented: you maintain a map of **approaches** (the different ways the incumbent could be improved) and decide where the effort goes next.

Two loops do the work. The **deep loop** (a Researcher, then Coders) runs experiments on the approaches you assign. The **wide loop** (a Mutator) makes undirected variations of whatever you hand it, and of nothing else: it never sees approaches or hypotheses, only artefacts and scores.

## The approach tree

Each approach has a state:
- `untried`: brainstormed, not tested yet;
- `promising`: something under it gained on validation. Gets the most effort, and is split into deeper sub-approaches;
- `unproven`: tried without a gain, but nothing shows it can't work. Retried occasionally, at lower priority. Bad scores are not proof;
- `pruned`: the engine verified a certificate that everything under it adds nothing. Never assigned again.

## Each generation, decide

1. **Brainstorm** new approaches when the map is thin or the promising ones are drying up. Make them genuinely different from each other, and add deeper sub-approaches under promising ones.
2. **Assign the Researcher** to approaches, each with a mode: `explore` (an untried approach), `exploit` (deepen a promising one), `probe` (a cheap experiment to learn whether an unproven one has anything).
3. **Hand the Mutator parents**: ids from the ledger to vary. The engine already gives two slots to the most important kept features (variants of kept features win far more often); you choose the rest. Spread those: width means variety across approaches. Near-misses and surprising scores are good parents.
4. **Combinations**: pairs of features that each gained on their own but weren't kept, to retry together (some things only help next to another). A pair with a member that showed no gain alone is skipped: in testing, such pairs never gained.
5. **Prune requests**: approaches you believe are dead. The Prover will try to certify it; only a verified certificate prunes.

Effort follows evidence, but keep a share for the unproven and the untried: a search that only exploits stops finding things.

## Reply format

Start with the JSON block, then at most 80 words on your reasoning.

```json
{"new_approaches": [{"title": "<short>", "description": "<one sentence>", "parent": "<approach id or empty>"}],
 "research": [{"approach": "<id, or the exact title of a new approach>", "mode": "explore | exploit | probe", "why": "<one line>"}],
 "mutate": {"vary": ["<id>", "..."], "fresh": <how many fresh slots>},
 "combine": [["<id>", "<id>"]],
 "prune": ["<approach id>"]}
```

## What a candidate is here: a feature

The incumbent is a policy, a weighted sum of features; approaches are kinds of measurements (what quantity, under which conditions). Mutator parents are feature ids.

# The problem: Forage: a drone collecting decaying items on a battery

A drone works on a square area (coordinates in [0, 1]) for 100 time units. Items appear over time at random places. Each item has a value when it appears, and its value falls linearly at the item's own rate (value units per time unit); when the value reaches 0 the item disappears. The drone flies in straight lines at speed 1 (one distance unit per time unit) and collects an item by flying to it: it gains the item's value at the moment it arrives, and the item is gone. Only the target is collected (flying over other items does not collect them).

The battery holds 1.0 (full). Flying drains `drain` per unit of distance; nothing else drains it. The battery recharges only at the charger: when the drone arrives at the charger it charges to full at `charge_rate` per time unit (taking (1 - battery) / charge_rate time units, during which time passes as usual). The drone starts at the charger with a full battery. If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).

## A feature

```python
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """One line: exactly what this measures."""
    ...
    return values   # one number per candidate
```

- `pos`: shape (2,), float: [x, y] of the drone now.
- `targets`: shape (k, 2), float: [x, y] of every candidate, in the (random) candidate order. The charger is one of the rows (at a random position); it is the row whose `values` is 0.
- `values`: shape (k,), float: the current value of each candidate item (always > 0 for an item); **0 for the charger**, so `values == 0` marks it.
- `rates`: shape (k,), float: how fast each item's value falls (value units per time unit; the item disappears after values / rates more time units); 0 for the charger.
- `battery`: float in [0, 1]: the battery left (1 = full).
- `drain`: float: battery used per unit of distance flown (a flight of length d needs d * drain).
- `charge_rate`: float: battery regained per time unit while charging at the charger.
- `charger`: shape (2,), float: [x, y] of the charger.
- `time`: float: the current time (from 0).
- `time_left`: float: time until the end.
- `history`: shape (s, 5), float: every item that has appeared so far (including those already collected or gone), in order of appearance: [x, y, time it appeared, value when it appeared, decay rate]. Nothing about items yet to appear.
- Return one finite number per candidate (shape (k,)), or a few columns (shape (k, c)). The highest-scoring candidate is the next target.
- Import only `numpy` and `math`. No state between calls, no randomness, don't modify the inputs, no Python loops over candidates when a vectorised form exists (features run thousands of times per evaluation). Guard every division and log.
- Return finite numbers, roughly in [-1, 1] (normalise; the optimiser rescales anyway).

## How the policy works

priority(candidate) = w1 * feature1 + w2 * feature2 + ...; the highest priority wins; on a tie, the first candidate wins. With no features every candidate scores 0, so the first candidate always wins: that is **Code Zero**, the starting point (0% progress). An optimiser fits the weights, including their signs. A new feature is kept only if the policy does better with it than the same refit without it, on training instances *and* on separate validation instances, and the gain isn't already given by the kept features.

## How policies are scored

Per instance, the **gap** is how far the solution is above a reference (lower is better). The score is the mean gap over families. **Progress** is the share of the way from Code Zero (0%) to the best reachable (100%).

# The problem: Forage: a drone collecting decaying items on a battery

A drone works on a square area (coordinates in [0, 1]) for 100 time units. Items appear over time at random places. Each item has a value when it appears, and its value falls linearly at the item's own rate (value units per time unit); when the value reaches 0 the item disappears. The drone flies in straight lines at speed 1 (one distance unit per time unit) and collects an item by flying to it: it gains the item's value at the moment it arrives, and the item is gone. Only the target is collected (flying over other items does not collect them).

The battery holds 1.0 (full). Flying drains `drain` per unit of distance; nothing else drains it. The battery recharges only at the charger: when the drone arrives at the charger it charges to full at `charge_rate` per time unit (taking (1 - battery) / charge_rate time units, during which time passes as usual). The drone starts at the charger with a full battery. If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).

# The problem: Forage: a drone collecting decaying items on a battery

A drone works on a square area (coordinates in [0, 1]) for 100 time units. Items appear over time at random places. Each item has a value when it appears, and its value falls linearly at the item's own rate (value units per time unit); when the value reaches 0 the item disappears. The drone flies in straight lines at speed 1 (one distance unit per time unit) and collects an item by flying to it: it gains the item's value at the moment it arrives, and the item is gone. Only the target is collected (flying over other items does not collect them).

The battery holds 1.0 (full). Flying drains `drain` per unit of distance; nothing else drains it. The battery recharges only at the charger: when the drone arrives at the charger it charges to full at `charge_rate` per time unit (taking (1 - battery) / charge_rate time units, during which time passes as usual). The drone starts at the charger with a full battery. If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).

# The problem: Forage: a drone collecting decaying items on a battery

A drone works on a square area (coordinates in [0, 1]) for 100 time units. Items appear over time at random places. Each item has a value when it appears, and its value falls linearly at the item's own rate (value units per time unit); when the value reaches 0 the item disappears. The drone flies in straight lines at speed 1 (one distance unit per time unit) and collects an item by flying to it: it gains the item's value at the moment it arrives, and the item is gone. Only the target is collected (flying over other items does not collect them).

The battery holds 1.0 (full). Flying drains `drain` per unit of distance; nothing else drains it. The battery recharges only at the charger: when the drone arrives at the charger it charges to full at `charge_rate` per time unit (taking (1 - battery) / charge_rate time units, during which time passes as usual). The drone starts at the charger with a full battery. If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).

# The problem: Forage: a drone collecting decaying items on a battery

A drone works on a square area (coordinates in [0, 1]) for 100 time units. Items appear over time at random places. Each item has a value when it appears, and its value falls linearly at the item's own rate (value units per time unit); when the value reaches 0 the item disappears. The drone flies in straight lines at speed 1 (one distance unit per time unit) and collects an item by flying to it: it gains the item's value at the moment it arrives, and the item is gone. Only the target is collected (flying over other items does not collect them).

The battery holds 1.0 (full). Flying drains `drain` per unit of distance; nothing else drains it. The battery recharges only at the charger: when the drone arrives at the charger it charges to full at `charge_rate` per time unit (taking (1 - battery) / charge_rate time units, during which time passes as usual). The drone starts at the charger with a full battery. If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).

    D = np.linalg.norm(targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :], axis=2)
    dch = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger, axis=1)
    reach = (b_after[:, None] - (D + dch[None, :]) * drain) > 0
    reach &= is_item[None, :]
    np.fill_diagonal(reach, False)
    vj = np.maximum(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * (d[:, None] + D), 0.0)
    look = (vj * reach).sum(axis=1) / norm
    out = np.clip(look / 3.0, -1.0, 1.0)

def _f016(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Negative normalised battery shortfall of the out-and-back trip (pos->target->charger), zero for the charger."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos, axis=1)
    dch = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger, axis=1)
    need = (d + dch) * drain

def _f012(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Value-per-flight-time, but only counting value that survives the trip, and conditioned on the trip being affordable so cheap far-away items don't win on a dying battery."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    is_charger = values <= 0
    # value that will still be there on arrival (never negative)
    arrival = np.maximum(values - rates * d, 0.0)
    # affordability: fraction of battery the trip consumes, saturating
    need = d * drain
    afford = np.clip(1.0 - need / np.maximum(battery, 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    # urgency of decay: how much of the horizon the item has left vs the trip
    life = np.where(rates > 0, values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9), 1e9)
    # perishable items get a boost when the trip eats a large share of their remaining life
    perish = np.clip(d / np.maximum(life, 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    scale = np.maximum(values.max(), 1e-9)
    s = (arrival / scale) * afford * (1.0 + perish) / (d + 0.2)
    return np.where(is_charger, 0.0, s)

# f014 feasible_arrival_value_roundtrip_amortised (wide): Arrival value amortised over the full battery cycle: flight out plus the trip back to the charger (and recharg
def _f014(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Arrival value amortised over the full battery cycle: flight out plus the trip back to the charger (and recharge time) needed to keep flying, so candidates far from the charger or draining a lot of battery are discounted; charger scores 1 - battery."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    is_charger = values <= 0
    d_charger = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)
    # total flight path if we go to the item and then must return to the charger
    tour = d + d_charger
    # battery spent on that tour
    spent = np.clip(tour * drain, 0.0, None)
    # recharge time needed to recover what was spent (after arriving at the charger)
    recharge = np.clip(spent / max(charge_rate, 1e-9), 0.0, None)
    # full cycle time: out, back, recharge
    cycle = tour + recharge
    # arrival value after decay during the outbound flight only
    arrival_val = np.maximum(values - rates * d, 0.0)
    # amortise over the cycle, guarding division
    eff = arrival_val / np.maximum(cycle, 1e-3)
    # normalise by the best achievable efficiency among items
    item_eff = np.where(is_charger, 0.0, eff)
    scale = np.maximum(item_eff.max(), 1e-9)
    # feasibility gate for the outbound leg
    feasible = (d * drain <= battery + 1e-9).astype(float)
    item_score = (item_eff / scale) * feasible
    charger_score = is_charger.astype(float) * (1.0 - battery)
    return item_score + charger_score

def _f028(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Max-decayed-value of any single other item reachable after picking this candidate (battery after arrival, then detour to that item and back to charger), minus the value-at-risk of the chosen candidate; charger row uses 1 - battery."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)          # pos -> each candidate
    is_item = values > 0
    D = np.linalg.norm(targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :], axis=2)  # candidate -> other
    dch = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)    # candidate -> charger
    b_after = battery - d * drain                               # battery at each candidate
    # reachability from candidate i to other item j and back to charger
    trip = D + dch[None, :]                                     # (i,j)
    reach = (b_after[:, None] - trip * drain) > 0
    reach &= is_item[None, :]
    np.fill_diagonal(reach, False)
    # decayed value of j at time we'd get there (via i)
    vj = np.maximum(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * (d[:, None] + D), 0.0)
    # best single follow-up item (not sum) -> focuses on the next good move
    masked = np.where(reach, vj, 0.0)
    best_follow = masked.max(axis=1) if masked.size else np.zeros(len(targets))
    norm = max(values.max(), 1e-9)
    follow = best_follow / norm

    # value-at-risk of the chosen candidate itself (how much it decays before arrival)
    arrival = np.maximum(values - rates * d, 0.0)
    risk = np.where(is_item, 1.0 - arrival / np.maximum(values, 1e-9), 0.0)

    item_score = np.clip(follow * 0.7 - risk * 0.5, -1.0, 1.0)
    charger_score = (~is_item).astype(float) * (1.0 - battery)
    return np.where(is_item, item_score, charger_score)

def _f027(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Negative shortfall of the out-and-back trip measured in recharge-time units (how long you'd be stuck recharging), gated to items only; zero for the charger and zero when the trip is affordable."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    dch = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)
    need = (d + dch) * drain
    shortfall_batt = np.maximum(need - battery, 0.0)
    # convert the battery shortfall into the wall-clock time it costs to recover it
    stuck_time = shortfall_batt / max(charge_rate, 1e-9)
    # also add the raw flight time that the shortfall implies (must detour via charger)
    extra_fly = shortfall_batt / max(drain, 1e-9)
    cost = stuck_time + extra_fly
    # normalise by a soft time scale: the whole horizon + a floor
    scale = max(time_left, 1.0) + 1.0
    feat = -np.clip(cost / scale, 0.0, 1.0)
    is_item = values > 0
    return np.where(is_item, feat, 0.0)

def _f042(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Min over the two legs of the best pair (c then j) of the slack life - travel time, clipped and zero for the charger."""
    k = targets.shape[0]
    is_item = values > 0
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)  # (k,)
    diff = targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :]     # (k, k, 2)
    D = np.linalg.norm(diff, axis=2)                     # (k, k)
    life = values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9)              # (k,)
    slack1 = life - d                                    # (k,)
    second = life[None, :] - (d[:, None] + D)            # (k, k)
    masked = np.where(np.eye(k, dtype=bool), -1e9, np.minimum(slack1[:, None], second))
    pair = masked.max(axis=1)                            # (k,)
    return np.where(is_item, np.clip(pair / 3.0, -1.0, 1.0), 0.0)

# f054 endgame_surviving_density (wide): Endgame density of value that still survives to arrival, minus the unreachable overshoot: arrival value per un
def _f054(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Endgame density of value that still survives to arrival, minus the unreachable overshoot: arrival value per unit time-to-reach, weighted by how much of the item's remaining life the trip consumes, zero outside the last stretch before the end."""
    k = targets.shape[0]
    is_item = values > 0
    d1 = np.sqrt(((targets - pos) ** 2).sum(axis=1))
    travel = np.maximum(d1, 1e-3)
    arrival = np.maximum(values - rates * travel, 0.0)
    # does the trip even finish before the episode ends? if not, it collects nothing
    finishes = (travel <= time_left).astype(float)
    # how much of the item's remaining life the trip eats (urgency)
    life = np.where(rates > 0, values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9), 1e9)
    life_share = np.clip(travel / np.maximum(life, 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    # density: surviving value per unit of time spent flying there, boosted when the trip eats the item's life
    dens = (arrival / travel) * (1.0 + life_share) * finishes
    dens = np.where(is_item, dens, 0.0)
    dens = np.where(np.isfinite(dens), dens, 0.0)
    dmax = dens.max() if k > 0 else 0.0
    # gate: only in the endgame window, and only meaningful if something is still capturable
    window = np.clip((8.0 - time_left) / 8.0, 0.0, 1.0)
    if dmax > 0.0 and window > 0.0:
        out = (dens / dmax) * window
    else:
        out = np.zeros(k)
    out = np.where(is_item, out, 0.0)
    return np.nan_to_num(out, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)

## What you get

- the **ledger** for the approaches you're assigned: what was tried, how it scored, and whether its prediction held;

## How to work

1. **Find a mechanism, not a symptom.** Name a concrete difference between the incumbent's results and the reference (or between what works and what doesn't), and the decision that produces it.
2. **Design experiments of two kinds:**

3. **Don't repeat the ledger.** If an idea was tried, change it meaningfully or leave it. A disguised copy is detected and discarded. When the ledger shows a group of tried features that behave alike, that idea is spent: look at a different quantity altogether.
4. **Learn from what failed.** A prediction that didn't hold means the mechanism you believed is wrong or incomplete. Say what it taught you (`lesson`) before proposing the next experiment.
5. **Predict.** Every experiment names one metric from the diagnostics, where it should move (a family or scope), and the direction. The engine checks it.

## What a candidate is here: a feature

The incumbent is a policy: a weighted sum of **features** (measurements of a candidate in one decision). An optimiser fits the weights and their signs, so never choose numbers or signs: choose *what to measure*. The parts in the sensitivity probes are the kept features; amplifying one means multiplying its weight.

- `change` is the exact measurement, per candidate, in terms of the arguments, so a Coder can write it without guessing. Say what it is for the last or special candidates when that matters.
- **It must rank candidates differently.** A value that is the same for every candidate in a decision, or a monotone copy of a feature the policy already has, tells the optimiser nothing. Prefer comparisons between normalised quantities; use a hard threshold only when the condition is the idea.
- A `probe` feature changes one thing, or exaggerates one aspect (a sharper threshold, a stronger form, one condition only).

A feature may apply only under a condition (only in some decisions, or for some candidates, when a quantity crosses a threshold) and be zero otherwise. The policy is one weighted sum, so a condition is the only way it can treat different cases differently.

# The problem: Forage: a drone collecting decaying items on a battery

A drone works on a square area (coordinates in [0, 1]) for 100 time units. Items appear over time at random places. Each item has a value when it appears, and its value falls linearly at the item's own rate (value units per time unit); when the value reaches 0 the item disappears. The drone flies in straight lines at speed 1 (one distance unit per time unit) and collects an item by flying to it: it gains the item's value at the moment it arrives, and the item is gone. Only the target is collected (flying over other items does not collect them).

The battery holds 1.0 (full). Flying drains `drain` per unit of distance; nothing else drains it. The battery recharges only at the charger: when the drone arrives at the charger it charges to full at `charge_rate` per time unit (taking (1 - battery) / charge_rate time units, during which time passes as usual). The drone starts at the charger with a full battery. If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).

## How the policy works

priority(candidate) = w1 * feature1 + w2 * feature2 + ...; the highest priority wins; on a tie, the first candidate wins. With no features every candidate scores 0, so the first candidate always wins: that is **Code Zero**, the starting point (0% progress). An optimiser fits the weights, including their signs. A new feature is kept only if the policy does better with it than the same refit without it, on training instances *and* on separate validation instances, and the gain isn't already given by the kept features.

## How policies are scored

Per instance, the **gap** is how far the solution is above a reference (lower is better). The score is the mean gap over families. **Progress** is the share of the way from Code Zero (0%) to the best reachable (100%).

# The problem: Forage: a drone collecting decaying items on a battery

A drone works on a square area (coordinates in [0, 1]) for 100 time units. Items appear over time at random places. Each item has a value when it appears, and its value falls linearly at the item's own rate (value units per time unit); when the value reaches 0 the item disappears. The drone flies in straight lines at speed 1 (one distance unit per time unit) and collects an item by flying to it: it gains the item's value at the moment it arrives, and the item is gone. Only the target is collected (flying over other items does not collect them).

The battery holds 1.0 (full). Flying drains `drain` per unit of distance; nothing else drains it. The battery recharges only at the charger: when the drone arrives at the charger it charges to full at `charge_rate` per time unit (taking (1 - battery) / charge_rate time units, during which time passes as usual). The drone starts at the charger with a full battery. If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).

## How the policy works

priority(candidate) = w1 * feature1 + w2 * feature2 + ...; the highest priority wins; on a tie, the first candidate wins. With no features every candidate scores 0, so the first candidate always wins: that is **Code Zero**, the starting point (0% progress). An optimiser fits the weights, including their signs. A new feature is kept only if the policy does better with it than the same refit without it, on training instances *and* on separate validation instances, and the gain isn't already given by the kept features.

## How policies are scored

Per instance, the **gap** is how far the solution is above a reference (lower is better). The score is the mean gap over families. **Progress** is the share of the way from Code Zero (0%) to the best reachable (100%).

```python
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Arrival value per unit of marginal detour (pos->target->charger minus direct pos->charger), gated by out-and-back battery feasibility; 0 for charger/infeasible."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos, axis=1)
    d2c = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger, axis=1)
    dpc = np.linalg.norm(pos - charger)
    detour = np.maximum(d + d2c - dpc, 0.0)
    arrival = np.maximum(values - rates * d, 0.0)
    feasible = (d + d2c) * drain <= battery + 1e-9
    score = np.where(values <= 0, 0.0, np.where(feasible, arrival / (detour + 0.05), 0.0))
    return score / (np.max(np.abs(score)) + 1e-9)
```

This computes each item's decayed arrival value divided by its marginal detour (the extra distance the out-and-back trip forces beyond the direct pos→charger leg, floored at 0 and smoothed by +0.05), zeroed for the charger and for battery-infeasible out-and-back trips, then normalised by the max absolute score; I read "detour" as the extra path length of pos→target→charger over pos→charger, and feasibility as the full out-and-back distance fitting in the current battery.

    """Best over follow-up items j of (decayed value of i plus decayed value of j) divided by the full cycle time pos->i->j->charger plus recharge time, gated on battery feasibility; 0 for the charger."""

    t_ij = d[:, None] + D                                       # (k,k)
    arr_j = np.maximum(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * t_ij, 0.0)  # (k,k)

    legs = d[:, None] + D + djc[None, :]                        # (k,k)

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Best over follow-up items j of (decayed value of i plus decayed value of j) divided by the full cycle time pos->i->j->charger plus recharge time, gated on battery feasibility; 0 for the charger."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)          # (k,)
    D = np.linalg.norm(targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :], axis=2)  # (k,k)
    djc = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)    # (k,)

    arr_i = np.maximum(values - rates * d, 0.0)                 # (k,)
    t_ij = d[:, None] + D                                       # (k,k)
    arr_j = np.maximum(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * t_ij, 0.0)  # (k,k)

    legs = d[:, None] + D + djc[None, :]                        # (k,k)
    need = legs * drain
    cycle = legs + need / charge_rate

    ratio = (arr_i[:, None] + arr_j) / (cycle + 0.1)

    valid = (values[None, :] > 0) & (~np.eye(len(values), dtype=bool)) & (need <= battery + 1e-9)
    ratio = np.where(valid, ratio, -1e9)

    best = np.max(ratio, axis=1)
    score = np.where(best <= -1e8, 0.0, best)
    score = np.where(values <= 0, 0.0, score)
    return score / (np.max(np.abs(score)) + 1e-9)

feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Value-per-unit-time from doing a full out-and-back-and-recharge cycle to this candidate, but only when that candidate can actually be reached directly; uses the round-trip viability (d + d_back) as the affordability gate instead of the one-way leg, and discounts by a concave (sqrt) rather than linear travel denominator."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    is_charger = values <= 0
    d_back = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)
    # round-trip affordability: how much of the battery a full cycle out and back actually needs
    need = (d + d_back) * drain
    afford = np.clip(1.0 - need / np.maximum(battery, 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    # value surviving the outbound flight
    arrival = np.maximum(values - rates * d, 0.0)
    # perishability: share of remaining life eaten by the outbound flight
    life = np.where(rates > 0, values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9), 1e9)
    perish = np.clip(d / np.maximum(life, 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    # concave travel denominator (diminishing penalty for distance) rather than linear
    denom = np.sqrt(np.maximum(d, 0.0) + 0.25)
    scale = np.maximum(values.max(), 1e-9)
    s = (arrival / scale) * afford * (1.0 + perish) / denom
    return np.where(is_charger, 0.0, np.nan_to_num(s, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0))

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Follow-up quality measured as the density (value per unit extra time) of the best reachable second item reached via the candidate, using the battery left after arrival at the candidate and a return-to-charger constraint, divided by the candidate's own time-since-arrival cost; charger row uses 1 - battery."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    is_item = values > 0
    D = np.linalg.norm(targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :], axis=2)
    dch = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)
    b_after = battery - d * drain
    trip = D + dch[None, :]
    reach = (b_after[:, None] - trip * drain) > 0
    reach &= is_item[None, :]
    np.fill_diagonal(reach, False)
    # decayed value of j at the moment we'd reach it via i
    vj = np.maximum(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * (d[:, None] + D), 0.0)
    # density of the follow-up: value per unit of extra travel time to reach j
    extra = np.maximum(D, 1e-3)
    dens = np.where(reach, vj / extra, 0.0)
    best_dens = dens.max(axis=1) if dens.size else np.zeros(len(targets))
    # normalise by the best density available this decision so magnitudes are comparable
    scale = max(best_dens.max(), 1e-9)
    follow = best_dens / scale

    # value-at-risk of the candidate itself (fraction lost before arrival)
    arrival = np.maximum(values - rates * d, 0.0)
    risk = np.where(is_item, 1.0 - arrival / np.maximum(values, 1e-9), 0.0)

    item_score = np.clip(follow - risk, -1.0, 1.0)
    charger_score = (~is_item).astype(float) * (1.0 - battery)
    return np.where(is_item, item_score, charger_score)

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Soft all-pairs future reachable value: instead of a hard battery-feasibility gate, each other item contributes its decayed value discounted by a softmax over battery margin and survival slack, so marginal trips count partially; normalised, charger row gets 1 - battery."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)  # pos -> candidate
    is_item = values > 0
    is_charger = ~is_item
    b_after = battery - d * drain                        # battery at candidate
    D = np.linalg.norm(targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :], axis=2)
    dch = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)
    # battery margin for the candidate -> j -> charger tour
    need = (D + dch[None, :]) * drain
    margin = (b_after[:, None] - need) / np.maximum(battery, 1e-6)
    # soft feasibility: sigmoid of margin (positive = can make the tour)
    feas = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-8.0 * margin))
    # survival slack: does j survive to the time we'd get there?
    life = np.where(rates > 0, values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9), 1e9)
    t_j = d[:, None] + D
    # value of j decayed to arrival, soft-clipped
    vj = np.maximum(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * t_j, 0.0)
    # also require j to still have life when we arrive (soft)
    survive = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-8.0 * (life[None, :] - t_j) / np.maximum(life[None, :], 1e-6)))
    contrib = vj * feas * survive
    contrib = np.where(is_item[None, :], contrib, 0.0)
    np.fill_diagonal(contrib, 0.0)
    # soft-sum (log-sum-exp style) so a few great follow-ups dominate a crowd of mediocre ones
    s = contrib.max(axis=1) if contrib.size else np.zeros(len(targets))
    total = contrib.sum(axis=1)
    norm = max(float(values.max()), 1e-9)
    look = (0.5 * total + 0.5 * s) / norm
    item_score = np.clip(look / 3.0, -1.0, 1.0)
    charger_score = is_charger.astype(float) * (1.0 - battery)
    return np.where(is_item, item_score, charger_score)

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Local crowding: for each candidate, the density of nearby still-valuable items relative to the flight time to sweep them, penalising candidates that sit in empty regions so the drone prefers targets embedded in clusters it can harvest on the way."""
    pos = np.asarray(pos, dtype=float)
    targets = np.asarray(targets, dtype=float)
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    rates = np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)
    charger = np.asarray(charger, dtype=float)
    k = targets.shape[0]
    is_item = values > 0

    d1 = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    D = np.linalg.norm(targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :], axis=2)
    np.fill_diagonal(D, np.inf)

    # radius that the drone could plausibly detour within: a fraction of what remains of the horizon
    reach_r = np.clip(0.15 + 0.25 * np.clip(time_left / 100.0, 0.0, 1.0), 0.05, 0.5)

    # decayed value of neighbours as if visited after the candidate (flight time d1 + D)
    vj = np.maximum(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * (d1[:, None] + D), 0.0)
    near = D <= reach_r
    near &= is_item[None, :]
    crowd = np.where(near, vj, 0.0).sum(axis=1)

    # time to sweep that neighbourhood approximated by the candidate's own arrival plus a small loop
    sweep = np.maximum(d1, 1e-3) + reach_r
    dens = crowd / sweep

    # normalise by best density so it's scale free
    scale = max(dens[is_item].max() if is_item.any() else 0.0, 1e-9)
    feat = np.where(is_item, dens / scale, 0.0)
    return np.nan_to_num(feat, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Battery-feasibility-adjusted arrival: net value after decay, gated by whether the flight can be made without running out."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    is_charger = values <= 0
    # time to reach, plus charging time if we end at charger
    travel = d
    # effective arrival value after decay during flight (never below 0)
    life = np.where(rates > 0, values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9), np.inf)
    arrival_val = np.maximum(values - rates * travel, 0.0)
    # feasibility: does the flight fit in the battery?
    need = d * drain
    feasible = (need <= battery).astype(float)
    # for charger candidate, treat as always feasible with value scaled by urgency (low battery good)
    charger_score = is_charger.astype(float) * (1.0 - battery)
    # normalise arrival value
    scale = np.maximum(values.max(), 1e-9)
    item_score = np.where(is_charger, 0.0, arrival_val / scale) * feasible
    return item_score + charger_score

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Value-per-flight-time, but only counting value that survives the trip, and conditioned on the trip being affordable so cheap far-away items don't win on a dying battery."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    is_charger = values <= 0
    # value that will still be there on arrival (never negative)
    arrival = np.maximum(values - rates * d, 0.0)
    # affordability: fraction of battery the trip consumes, saturating
    need = d * drain
    afford = np.clip(1.0 - need / np.maximum(battery, 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    # urgency of decay: how much of the horizon the item has left vs the trip
    life = np.where(rates > 0, values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9), 1e9)
    # perishable items get a boost when the trip eats a large share of their remaining life
    perish = np.clip(d / np.maximum(life, 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    scale = np.maximum(values.max(), 1e-9)
    s = (arrival / scale) * afford * (1.0 + perish) / (d + 0.2)
    return np.where(is_charger, 0.0, s)

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Arrival value amortised over the full battery cycle: flight out plus the trip back to the charger (and recharge time) needed to keep flying, so candidates far from the charger or draining a lot of battery are discounted; charger scores 1 - battery."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    is_charger = values <= 0
    d_charger = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)

    tour = d + d_charger
    # battery spent on that tour
    spent = np.clip(tour * drain, 0.0, None)
    # recharge time needed to recover what was spent (after arriving at the charger)
    recharge = np.clip(spent / max(charge_rate, 1e-9), 0.0, None)
    # full cycle time: out, back, recharge
    cycle = tour + recharge
    # arrival value after decay during the outbound flight only
    arrival_val = np.maximum(values - rates * d, 0.0)
    # amortise over the cycle, guarding division
    eff = arrival_val / np.maximum(cycle, 1e-3)
    # normalise by the best achievable efficiency among items
    item_eff = np.where(is_charger, 0.0, eff)
    scale = np.maximum(item_eff.max(), 1e-9)
    # feasibility gate for the outbound leg
    feasible = (d * drain <= battery + 1e-9).astype(float)
    item_score = (item_eff / scale) * feasible
    charger_score = is_charger.astype(float) * (1.0 - battery)
    return item_score + charger_score
feature.measures: Arrival value amortised over the full battery cycle: flight out plus the trip back to the charger (and recharge time) needed to keep flying, so candidates far from the charger or draining a lot of battery are discounted; charger scores 1 - battery.

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Negative shortfall of the out-and-back trip measured in recharge-time units (how long you'd be stuck recharging), gated to items only; zero for the charger and zero when the trip is affordable."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    dch = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)
    need = (d + dch) * drain
    shortfall_batt = np.maximum(need - battery, 0.0)
    # convert the battery shortfall into the wall-clock time it costs to recover it
    stuck_time = shortfall_batt / max(charge_rate, 1e-9)
    # also add the raw flight time that the shortfall implies (must detour via charger)
    extra_fly = shortfall_batt / max(drain, 1e-9)
    cost = stuck_time + extra_fly
    # normalise by a soft time scale: the whole horizon + a floor
    scale = max(time_left, 1.0) + 1.0
    feat = -np.clip(cost / scale, 0.0, 1.0)
    is_item = values > 0
    return np.where(is_item, feat, 0.0)

feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Max-decayed-value of any single other item reachable after picking this candidate (battery after arrival, then detour to that item and back to charger), minus the value-at-risk of the chosen candidate; charger row uses 1 - battery."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)          # pos -> each candidate
    is_item = values > 0
    D = np.linalg.norm(targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :], axis=2)  # candidate -> other
    dch = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)    # candidate -> charger
    b_after = battery - d * drain                               # battery at each candidate
    # reachability from candidate i to other item j and back to charger
    trip = D + dch[None, :]                                     # (i,j)
    reach = (b_after[:, None] - trip * drain) > 0
    reach &= is_item[None, :]
    np.fill_diagonal(reach, False)
    # decayed value of j at time we'd get there (via i)
    vj = np.maximum(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * (d[:, None] + D), 0.0)
    # best single follow-up item (not sum) -> focuses on the next good move
    masked = np.where(reach, vj, 0.0)
    best_follow = masked.max(axis=1) if masked.size else np.zeros(len(targets))
    norm = max(values.max(), 1e-9)
    follow = best_follow / norm

    # value-at-risk of the chosen candidate itself (how much it decays before arrival)
    arrival = np.maximum(values - rates * d, 0.0)
    risk = np.where(is_item, 1.0 - arrival / np.maximum(values, 1e-9), 0.0)

    item_score = np.clip(follow * 0.7 - risk * 0.5, -1.0, 1.0)
    charger_score = (~is_item).astype(float) * (1.0 - battery)
    return np.where(is_item, item_score, charger_score)
